name: May 17, 2022 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MAY 17,2022
  VARIOUS TELECONFERENCE LOCATIONS
  5:30P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Peak called the meeting to order at 5:36 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Alicia Peak; Vice Chair Dane Skophammer; and Commissioners
  Georgia Goldfarb and Cayley Jenner

  ABSENT: Commissioner Suzanne Guldimann

  ALSO PRESENT: Jesse Bobbett, Community Services Director; Kristin Riesgo,
  Community Services Deputy Director; Kate Gallo, Recreation Manager; Chris Orosz,
  Recreation Supervisor; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Peak led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Goldfarb moved, and Commissioner Jenner seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,
  Commissioner Guldimann absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on May 13, 2022.

ITEMl  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Administration of Oath to Newly Appointed Commissioner

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua administered the Oath of Office to
  Commissioner Goldfarb.

  B.  Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award Video Recognition

  Community Services Director Bobbett shared a recognition video of the 2021 Jake
  Kuredjian Citizenship Award recipients.

  In response to Chair Peak, Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo stated the
  video would be shared on social media and added to the City's website.

ITEM2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Robert Gold stated he provided Community Services Director Bobbett with details
  on his concerns regarding the Permanent Skate Park and requested the Commission
  to review the email. Mr. Gold stated he had concerns related to the Permanent Skate
  Park design and issues following the daily operation of the Temporary Skate Park.

ITEM3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Chair Peak moved, and Commissioner Jenner seconded a motion to approve the
  Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,
  Commissioner Guldimann absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the April 19, 2022 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  during April 2022.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Trancas Open Space Non-Native Vegetation
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report on the removal of non-native
  vegetation at the Trancas Open Space.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz presented the staff report.
   Parks and Recreation Commission

  Page 3 of 6

  In response to Chair Peak, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated the bulky items were
  dumped in Priority Area 1.

  In response to Chair Peak, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated the bi-annual site
  review was sufficient since crews removed all Castor Bean and Tree Tobacco
  plants. He stated staff would install "No Dumping" signs on Trancas Canyon Road,
  and staff would monitor illegal dumping.

  Commissioner Goldfarb expressed her concerns regarding the number of foxtail
  plants.

  In response to Commissioner Jenner, Community Services Director Bobbett stated
  homeless encampments were not discovered on the property.

MOTION  Commissioner Goldfarb moved, and Vice Chair Skophammer seconded a motion
  to receive and file the Trancas Open Space Non-Native Vegetation Report. The
  question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Commissioner Guldimann absent.

  B.  Sunscreen Station Program
  Recommended Action: Review the BrightGuard Sunscreen Station Program and
  provide direction to staff.

  Recreation Manager Gallo presented the staff report.

  Alexander Beck provided information on the sunscreen station program and
  BrightGuard's partnership with UCLA Health. He stated the cancer prevention
  program was for Malibu residents and visitors.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Manager Gallo stated the
  BrightGuard proposal included the installation of sunscreen stations at Malibu
  Bluffs Park, Legacy Park, Las Flores Park, Trancas Canyon Park, Equestrian Park,
  Legacy Park, and the Malibu Community Pool. She stated staff recommended
  installing sunscreen stations at two supervised facilities, Malibu Bluffs Park and
  the Malibu Community Pool.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Manager Gallo stated she
  worked with Mr. Beck to provide sunscreen stations similar to hand sanitizing
  stations. She stated BrightGuard's proposed stations violated regulations in the
  Malibu Municipal Code.

  Chair Peak suggested a sunscreen station at Trancas Canyon Park.

  Commissioner Jenner indicated agreement with Chair Peak and suggested
  installing it inside the restrooms.
   Parks and Recreation Commission

  Page4 of6

  Chair Peak stated installation could occur from Memorial Day to Labor Day.

  In response to Vice Chair Skophammer, Recreation Manager Gallo stated
  BrightGuard would be responsible for maintenance, weekly monitoring, and
  refilling the stations for the duration of the Agreement.

  Mr. Beck stated he hoped the program could continue for multiple years in Malibu.
  He stated he worked with the City of Santa Monica from Memorial Day to Labor
  Day, and the program temporarily shut down for two years due to COVID-19.

  In response to Vice Chair Skophammer, Mr. Beck stated UCLA Health funds the
  program, and the sunscreen was not available over the counter.

  In response to Chair Peak, Mr. Beck stated the City of Santa Monica had sunscreen
  stations at various locations from 2017 to 2019, and there were few instances of
  vandalism. He stated he would remove sunscreen stations that were vandalized
  more than two times.

  Chair Peak recommended staff work with Mr. Beck to install sunscreen stations at
  Trancas Canyon Park, Malibu Bluffs Park, and the Malibu Community Pool.

MOTION  Commissioner Goldfarb moved, and Commissioner Jenner seconded a motion to
  install two sunscreen stations at Malibu Bluffs Park, one sunscreen station at the
  Malibu Community Pool, and one sunscreen station at Trancas Canyon Park from
  July I through September 5, 2022. The question was called, and the motion carried
  4-0, Commissioner Guldimann absent.

  C.  Earth Friendly Management Policy Quarterly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report regarding Earth Friendly
  Management Policy activities for the months of January to March 2022.

  Community Services Director Bobbett presented the staff report.

  In response to Chair Peak, Community Services Director Bobbett stated City
  properties were managed differently depending on the on-site facilities and
  intended use of the park. He stated the quarterly report would focus on exclusion
  and education.

MOTION  Chair Peak moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion to receive and
  file the Earth Friendly Management Policy report regarding activities for the
  months of January to March 2022. The question was called, and the motion carried
  4-0, Commissioner Guldimann absent.

ITEM6  STAFF UPDATES

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz provided an update on erosion mitigation and trail
  maintenance at Charrnlee Wilderness Park.

  The Commission viewed the spring trail camera video.

  Community Services Director Bobbett stated staff would publish the trail camera
  video on social media.

  Recreation Manager Gallo provided an update on aquatic programs, the Summer
  Recreation Guide, and summer day camp registration.

  Community Services Director Bobbett provided an update on staff assignments
  from the Commission.

ITEM7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Goldfarb thanked staff for their work and expressed appreciation for
  the completed work at Trancas Open Space.

  Vice Chair Skophammer stated he was disappointed the tow yard was temporarily
  located at the Heathercliffproperty.

  Commissioner Goldfarb indicated agreement with Vice Chair Skophammer.

  Chair Peak stated visitors were parking in the fire Jane at Malibu Bluffs Park on
  Saturdays.

  In response to Chair Peak, Community Services Director Bobbett stated rattlesnake
  signs could be installed at city parks with a quick response (QR) code to an
  educational video on snake safety.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 7:25 p.m., Chair Peak moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion
  to adjourn the meeting. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,
  Commissioner Guldimann absent.

  Approved and adopted by the Parks and
  Recreation Commission of the City of
  Malibu on June 21, 2022.
